notes: Fixtures are self-contained (see fixtures/make_fixtures.py) so runs do not depend on the user's Slack/Gmail/Drive being reachable. Author persona: Dana Reyes - lowercase commit subjects, em dashes, bold labels, owns mistakes, hedges on next steps. Per-eval `files` is a hard contract enforced by setup_runs.py - iteration 1 initially copied every fixture into every run directory, which invalidated the no-samples case and put the reference answer next to the humanize case.

evals.name: voice-match-from-git
evals.prompt: I'm about to commit a fix in the fernpost-api repo. I changed the pagination cursor so the limit param is actually respected when a filter is applied - before, passing a filter would quietly return the whole result set. Write the commit message for me.
evals.expected_output: A commit message matching Dana's git voice: lowercase subject with no trailing period, a body that says why it mattered rather than restating the diff, and the hedging/ownership habit visible. Just the message - no narration of the search.

assertions.text: Subject line is lowercase (matches all 8 prior commits)
Subject line has no trailing period
Body explains why the bug mattered, not just what changed
Output is the commit message itself, not a report on how sources were searched
check_ai_tells.py scan exits 0 (no mechanical tells)

evals.name: humanize-preserving-habits
evals.prompt: This Q3 update draft reads like a robot wrote it - can you rewrite it so it sounds like me? My past updates are in slack-history.md. The draft is q3-draft-slop.md.
evals.expected_output: AI tells removed (testament/pivotal/underscore vocabulary, inline-header bullets, negative parallelism, Title Case heading, chatbot sign-off, formulaic challenges section) WHILE retaining Dana's genuine habits - em dashes and bold labels both appear in her real Slack history and must survive.

assertions.text: AI vocabulary removed: no 'testament', 'pivotal', 'underscore', 'myriad', 'seamless', 'foster'
Chatbot sign-off 'I hope this helps' / 'Let me know if' removed
Negative parallelism ('not just X, it's Y') removed
Inline-header bullet list ('- **Synchronization:** ...') removed or restructured
PRESERVES em dashes - they are in Dana's baseline at 31/1k and are not an AI tell for her
PRESERVES lowercase-prose or bold-label habit visible in her Slack history
Output is the rewritten draft, not a changelog of edits made
Retains all three items from the SOURCE DRAFT (dedupe, retries, caching) - checked against the draft, not the author's history, since the skill's rule is carry voice not content

evals.notes: A length floor was tried and removed: it rewards padding, and a thin source honestly rewritten is legitimately short. Substance is checked by item coverage (b7) instead.

evals.name: no-samples-fallback
evals.prompt: Write a short internal announcement telling the team that the Friday deploy window is moving to Tuesday mornings starting next month, because Friday incidents keep eating people's weekends. Two or three paragraphs.
evals.expected_output: Composes without any retrievable samples. Must not claim to have read the user's past writing, must not fabricate sources, must still avoid slop, and must not be so neutral it reads as generated.

assertions.text: Does not claim to have read or matched the user's past writing
Does not fabricate source links or file paths
check_ai_tells.py scan exits 0 (no mechanical tells)
States the actual reason (weekend incidents) rather than vague 'operational excellence' framing

evals.name: over-correction-guard
evals.prompt: Give q3-draft-clean.md a once-over before I post it. My past updates are in slack-history.md.
evals.expected_output: The draft is already clean and already in Dana's voice. The correct behavior is to leave it substantially alone - not to 'improve' it into neutral corporate prose, and specifically not to strip the lowercase style or em dashes that are her actual habits.

assertions.text: Does not rewrite wholesale - output retains majority of original wording
PRESERVES em dashes present in the original
PRESERVES the lowercase prose style of the original
Does not introduce AI vocabulary or inline-header bullets that were not there
Any changes proposed are specific and few, not a full reflow

evals.notes: git history is included deliberately: verifying a factual claim in the draft against the commit log is realistic behavior for this skill, and the iteration-1 run did exactly that.
